newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay shares end two pct lower, ACC leads slide.
newsitem.headline: Bombay shares end two pct lower, ACC leads slide.

text.p: ** Bombay's shares end lower on Wednesday with cement and auto firms leading the slide, traders say
** Shares of cement firm ACC crash below 1,000 rupees after disastrous first half results stun market, rebound slightly near close as some punters cover positions
** Bombay's stocks index falls 62.30 points or 2.11 percent to close at provisional 2886.14; off low of 2847.48
** Punters hammer prices across-the board, funds put hold on buy orders as investors wait to see where the index is headed
** National Stock Exchange activates circuit breaker in several key stocks during the day
Bombay shares ended lower in a volatile session on Wednesday with auto and cement stocks leading the slide, traders said.
"Short covering at the end pulled prices slightly higher but there was a conspicuous absence of buyers during the day," said a chief dealer at a foreign brokerage.
"Large investors don't feel good about this market."
Bombay's benchmark stocks index fell 62.30 points or 2.11 percent to end at a provisional 2886.14, off a low of 2847.48
The National Stock Exchange (NSE) index shed 18.83 points to a provisional 829.91.
India's largest cement maker ACC led the slide, plunging 138 rupees or 13.11 percent to 1,018 rupees, off a low of 980.

ACC said on Tuesday its net profit fell 56 percent to 550.5 million rupees in the first six months to September 30, 1996 against 1.25 billion rupees. The firm said it could not recover an unprecedented increase in input cost, affecting margins.
Expectations had ranged from 800 to 900 million rupees.
Traders said the market had not discounted an impending oil price hike which was needed to curb India's oil pool deficit.
"A price hike of the magnitude necessary to affect the oil deficit will again hit second half results," the trader said.
Frontline auto firms TELCO, Bajaj Auto and Mahindra & Mahindra -- which have recently been pounded lower on fears of a prolonged economic slowdown -- continued to head southward.
Some analysts have recommended investors go underweight on the sector but others said they remained bullish on auto.
"Sales growth continues to stay above 20 percent and next fiscal is likely to see a recovery. The extent of the slowdown has been exaggerated," said an analyst at a foreign brokerage.
He said he maintained his buy recommendations on these three stocks.
-- Priya Ramani, Bombay newsroom +91-22-265 9000
